correctness.rationale: Dirichlet(1,...,1) joint survival probabilities yield all moments by exact integration; derivative of variance equals minus twice covariance. The auxiliary ratio b^(n-1)/a^(2n-1) rises then falls, which proves the single strict finite-n sign switch for n≥3, with n=2 handled separately. Uniform expansion at s=c/n and an isolated simple positive limiting root prove the sharp n^-1 correction; the rational/numerical standalone script independently checks finite identities and parameters, not serving as proof.

originality.rationale: For the final narrow claim, inspected Huillet full text gives more general marginal vacancy law, making the raw moment calculation already implied. Its inspected statement and proof do not assert the all-n unique strict variance maximum, gap–vacancy sign change, or first optimizing-density correction. Six actual dedicated semantic published-finding corpus queries returned no equivalent; nearby records concern different models. Older joint-limit and variance references incompletely accessible are explicitly listed as risks. The PASS is a qualified best-knowledge judgment only, not a proof of priority.
residual_risks: The 1984 full text by Holst and Hüsler was not available for line-by-line assessment; its abstract states joint limits, not the exact finite-size strict maximizer, but an equivalent theorem cannot be excluded.
The full 1984 Huffer technical report and Pitts 1981 article could not be inspected; they could contain a transformed variance-unimodality statement.

The published complete marginal distribution of vacant length implies each finite-n variance after integration; the originality of the strict unimodality theorem rests on a new qualitative analysis of this derivable expression, not on claiming the formula itself is absent from prior mathematics.

value.rationale: For the basic homogeneous random circle-coverage model, gives for every finite sample size one and only one optimal arc length maximizing uncovered-area variance, plus a complete counterintuitive sign reversal in gap-count/length dependence and explicit asymptotic optimal sensor density. Distinguishes maximal average coverage from maximal uncertainty and sharpens classical marginal distribution findings. No generalization is claimed to unequal or random arc lengths.
